data.narrative:
Atom Computing is a Series B quantum computing company that has raised over $300M to date. The quantum computing sector comprises 11 identifiable peers—3 public companies (IonQ, Rigetti, D-Wave) and 8 private firms including Quantinuum, PsiQuantum, and SandboxAQ—though the private subset remains fragmented across distinct technology approaches and development stages.

A peer-median triangulation proved inapplicable due to insufficient same-stage or adjacent-stage comparables within quantum computing; the sector lacks the density of similarly-positioned Series B companies needed for robust benchmarking. Accordingly, analysis relied on stage-progression methodology, applying a 1.9x step-up multiplier typical of Series B advancement to the $300M raised baseline, yielding an implied valuation of $570M. This single-method triangulation carries inherent constraints given the narrow applicability set.

The analysis supports a valuation range of $484M to $656M, with a median point of $570M. Material uncertainties include the absence of direct Series B comparables in quantum computing, which limits confidence in the stage multiplier, and the heterogeneity of approaches across the broader peer set, making cross-sector benchmarking unreliable. Additional data on quantum hardware metrics, customer traction, or pathway to commercialization would strengthen conviction in this range.
